messages:
nina: hey team, new here — running our e2e suite in CI using a sandbox key and we27re seeing intermittent 429s only when the matrix runs parallel. Any quick wins besides slowing down tests?
josh: welcome! :wave: sandbox quotas are intentionally small. quick wins: add exponential backoff + jitter, and reuse a single token across the matrix when possible (repo secret).
nina: we already share the same repo secret, but still spikes when 12 jobs hit at once. backoff helped some but still flaky.
devex-bot: Tip: consider a lightweight response cache or record/replay for non-flaky endpoints. See https://docs.redwood.ai/dev-keys#ci-patterns for patterns.
infra: if you need concurrent throughput for a short window we can provision a temporary sandbox quota bump. Send repo name + run window + expected concurrency. We27ll create a ticket.
ina: that would be great. is there a standard request format?
infra: yes, send to #eng-infra or email infra@redwood.ai with: project, repo, CI provider, runner count, start/end times. We prefer 2-4 hour windows for e2e.
ci-bot: Also: monitor X-RateLimit-Remaining header in responses to detect approaching limits. Example header: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 42
josh: another option: mock only the LLM calls in unit-heavy tests and reserve a small smoke e2e job to validate integration against sandbox. That reduces quota usage significantly.
sam: FYI, for prod-like heavy load testing we use Dedicated reserved capacity tokens in a staging org. Devex can help onboard you.
nina: thanks all. infra — I27ll DM repo + time window. Also will add jittered backoff and header logging to our test runner. Any naming convention for secrets you recommend?
devex-bot: Use STAGING_REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY or CI_REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY. Keep hosted keys out of CI unless it's prod.
infra: ticket created: INF-2026. You27re in the queue for a temporary bump tomorrow 09:00-11:00 UTC.
nina: amazing, thanks! saved me from adding artificial sleeps :relieved:
